notes.title: Development Update: Building Dimraeth’s Unique Visual Style
notes.notes:
[p]Heya! I’m Vancris Balanon, Art Director of Dimraeth. Today I want to take you behind the scenes of something the whole art team poured our hearts into: crafting The World of Dimraeth. From the smallest blade of grass in the Wildwood Forest to the colossal statues of the Old Ones, every detail was carefully considered.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/1027440743fa2c89a4ed54d5beb3196840fc066a.png"][/img][/p][p][b]The Three Guiding Pillars of Environment[/b][/p][p]Creating a world from scratch is no small feat—it was easily one of the toughest challenges our art team faced. But those challenges brought incredible satisfaction when everything clicked. To guide us, we focused on three pillars: Unique Visual Identity, Immersion, and Game Design Alignment. In this post, we’ll dive into the first pillar.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/69ead3f3a8b9f75226d85796da27fc4c5f200f95.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Why Unique Visual Identity Matters[/b][/p][p]For us, a strong visual identity means players will remember an environment long after they’ve left it. But what creates that sense of uniqueness? Two key elements: Biome and Culture.[/p][p][/p][p]The best example is Earlwood Village, the player’s very first glimpse of the outside world. We wanted it to feel simple yet breathtaking—a quiet seaside settlement at the edge of the continent, far from the bustling cities of Mirkea, but unforgettable in its own right.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/6974c997caa8af93bca5bd0c49872121582d6f52.png"][/img][/p][p][b]The Earlwood Peninsula[/b][/p][p]To achieve this, we started with geography. Location is the foundation of any environment, so we looked to real-world wonders for inspiration: the White Cliffs of Dover, the Fingal Caves of Scotland, and Vietnam’s Ghềnh Đá Đĩa. Right away, it was clear Earlwood belonged on a dramatic coastal landscape like these. So we crafted a geographical location from these inspirations and produced matching fauna and flora. Earlwood Peninsula was born.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/9d3fe6a09c578c078962174d9223ecc369f527db.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]The People of Earlwood[/b][/p][p]With geography set, we turned to culture. The villagers draw on human traditions from Aldoria with a touch of Elven influence from their neighbors in the Eternal Forest. Their coastal home naturally shapes their way of life, which revolves around fishing, farming, logging, and trade.[/p][p][/p][p]Even their architecture reflects this connection. Homes and tools reuse materials salvaged from shipwrecks along the Earlwood Cliffs or repurposed parts from old boat production. Every detail was refined alongside our narrative director to make sure it all tied into the village’s history and the broader world of Dimraeth.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/4443594a0b8cef61bd95ddad671cafdbb0573e3b.png"][/img][/p][p][b]Earlwood's Visual Identity[/b][/p][p]After countless sketches, iterations, and discussions, Earlwood’s Unique Visual Identity came to life. It’s the perfect introduction to the wider world of Dimraeth—and a first step we hope players will never forget.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/d3e6ca709a8a42693d74df8d692009b3ec24e096.png"][/img][/p][p]That wraps up Pillar One! Next time, we’ll dive into Immersion—how we make Dimraeth feel alive and picturesque. Stay tuned for the next devlog! 
[/p]

notes.title: Development Update: Crafting Combat in Dimraeth
notes.notes:
[p]Hi everyone, Phillip here, Game Director on [i]Dimraeth[/i].[/p][p]In today’s devlog, I want to dive into the combat of Dimraeth including our inspirations, our design pillars, and how we’re crafting a system that rewards precision, planning, and team synergy.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/c89e920250857a9118f4d0fb4a88ce3eb0c61745.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]The Combat of Dimraeth: A Fusion of Tension and Tactics[/b][/h3][p]As a designer, I like to wear my inspirations on my sleeve, so let’s go through some of our inspirations. Dimraeth’s combat is born of numerous inspirations such as Roguelikes like [i]Hades[/i] and [i]Ravenwatch[/i], MOBA-style spell systems, and a touch of [i]Soulslike[/i] tension. We knew from day one that we didn’t want traditional top-down ARPG combat with endless hordes and ability spam.[/p][p][/p][p]Instead, our goal is tactical action that [i]feels[/i] good moment-to-moment, with room for creativity and mastery whether you're playing solo or in co-op.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/63636db23e8255ffcd64c9f2ca8e052f18a2d4d6.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Core Mechanics: Flow and Flexibility[/b][/h3][p]Combat in Dimraeth is built around three central pillars: defense, attacks, and spells. Every character comes equipped with a standard dash and a race-specific guard, each with their own cooldown. At the same time, enemies signal their attacks with readable wind-ups and clear tells. Whether you can react in time—dashing, guarding, or committing to an attack—often determines the outcome of the fight. Unless you’re running a heavy-defense build, every hit you take comes at a cost. And keep in mind: dodging, blocking, casting, and striking all consume stamina, so you’ll need to manage your choices carefully.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/a0451b8acc2a3e8499fa5e83836bb96244955896.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Basic Attacks Matter[/b][/h3][p]Basic attacks aren't just filler. Each race has its own combo chain (3-4 hits) that creates a rhythm in combat. Even for magic-heavy builds, these attacks remain useful late-game thanks to on-hit passives and synergies.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/a585c4f58711a0543ed8e27e2d1958acced3d1ca.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Spells and Buildcrafting[/b][/h3][p]Spells are the foundation of your combat identity in Dimraeth. At launch, we aim to offer over 300 spells, designed around chain interactions and status synergy to allow for rich and expressive builds. Though you’ll have many spells to choose from, your equipped slots are limited, so selecting the right set becomes a strategic decision.[/p][p][/p][p]Do you ignite enemies with fire and follow up with an inferno? Stack bleed effects with your teammate to trigger an execution finisher? Layer frost on an enemy and then freeze them in place with a javelin of ice? Every spell is part of a greater puzzle—each one a piece of possibility, not a one-off button.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/bc6e236a181eed3a28b537abaf3e28c34f1f2597.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Smarter Enemies, Better Fights[/b][/h3][p]We’ve designed Dimraeth’s enemy AI using a token-based system inspired by God of War and Ghost of Tsushima. This system ensures that enemies fight in waves and with coordination, rather than chaotic mob-rushing. You’ll find genuine openings to react to, not just spam to endure. Whether you’re facing down a giant treant, a spell-casting dryad, or a fast-moving wolf pack—timing and spacing are everything. If you’re planning to cast a long-windup spell, make sure you’ve actually got the window for it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/8ca17ac6e71f3f4e5206fc8e44574f328bba3aaa.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Boss Battles: Where it All Comes Together[/b][/h3][p]Boss fights are a defining part of the Dimraeth experience. Whether you’re going in alone or as a group, each boss encounter brings intensity, complexity, and a sense of triumph. These fights test your reaction speed, your build decisions, and your grasp of the system as a whole. Each boss is built with unique mechanics and deadly abilities—and what they offer in return isn’t just loot, but the satisfaction of overcoming a challenge. And when you beat a boss alongside friends, it becomes more than just victory—it becomes a memory.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/a3558537ec58a5f9dee3c2a420fb1f8ce2dcc4f2.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Looking Ahead[/b][/h3][p]This was just a taste of the combat we’re building in [i]Dimraeth[/i]. There’s more to come, boss fights, weapon skills, rare modifiers, and more.[/p][p][/p][p]If you're curious to try it for yourself, keep an eye on our socials—we’ve got something exciting coming soon.[/p][p][/p][p]Until then, Phillip signing off.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Development Update: Greetings from Earlwood!
notes.notes:
[p]Hello all. Phillip here, Game Director on [i]Dimraeth[/i].[/p][p][/p][p]This is likely the first time you’ve heard from me directly. As we move toward release, I’ll be posting regular updates: glimpses of the world taking shape, the game loop, and the stories we hope you’ll soon step into.[/p][p][/p][p]For this first devlog, I want to introduce the first town region players will explore: [b]Earlwood Village[/b]. A place of beauty and tragedy, and a fitting beginning for your journey through [i]Dimraeth[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/82f0fc3c23977cadb98fb0a675e85e6c9518954f.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Between Kingdom and Forest: A Place of Outcasts[/b][/h3][p]Earlwood is unlike many places in [b]Mirkea[/b]. It stands on the border between the Human Kingdom of [b]Aldoria[/b] and the vast [b]Eternal Forest[/b], home of the elves.[/p][p][/p][p]Three centuries ago, it began as a lone homestead. Over time it became something more—a refuge for those cast out of their own lands. Here you’ll find [b]Minotaurs[/b], [b]Elves[/b], [b]Dwarves[/b], and [b]Humans[/b], bound not by blood or crown, but by circumstance.[/p][p][/p][p]Earlwood is a town of outcasts, of those seeking a second life. That fragile kind of community carries its own quiet beauty.[/p][p][/p][p]Earlwood was one of the first regions we built during early development. It anchors the opening act of the game, a place where the first threads of the story are woven.[/p][p][/p][p]We wanted this first town to feel layered: warm and welcoming on the surface, but marked by deeper wounds beneath. Most of [b]Mirkea[/b] remains divided along ancient lines. Earlwood stands apart. Here, for a time, those divisions have faded.[/p][p][/p][p]But such peace is never simple. And when players arrive, they’ll find the village already caught in a slow unraveling.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/699c0abdecacd909e9b0b5c27d6e460f231753b1.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]A Forest, a Kingdom of its own[/b][/h3][p]The [b]Wildwood[/b] that surrounds Earlwood is no ordinary forest. Though it lies at the border of the vast [b]Eternal Forest[/b], it is not ruled by Elves, nor claimed by the Kingdom of Aldoria.[/p][p][/p][p]Here, each stretch of forest is its own domain. The Wildwood is a fractured land of many small kingdoms, each ruled by a [b]Forest King[/b]—ancient spirits of nature, be they [b]Dryads[/b], [b]Treants[/b], or stranger powers still. Though divided, they are bound by one law: the will of [b]Ceres[/b], the nature god whose laws shape all life beneath the canopy.[/p][p][/p][p]The balance between the Wildwood and Earlwood Village is delicate. In ages past, the elders of Earlwood understood the forest’s ways, maintaining an uneasy accord. Now, that knowledge is fading—known only to a dwindling few, while the forest remembers far more than men do.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/e20e600aa6eddc16f275f67c7753ccc8b7b0bfe2.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Tragedy and Hope[/b][/h3][p]Finding the right tone for Earlwood has been one of the more delicate parts of its design. It is a cozy village of outcasts. A place where players should feel welcome. Yet when they arrive, the village stands on the brink of crisis.[/p][p][/p][p]Fear has gripped the town. Most quarters are sealed. The guards allow no one through. But not all obey. The [b]Guild Hall Quarter[/b] remains open. It serves both as a refuge for the displaced and the village’s last hope of defense.[/p][p][/p][p]Here, we want players to feel the tension. The weight of what has been lost. The hope that still holds. [/p][p]In [i]Dimraeth[/i], we aim to build a world that invites you in with clarity and color, while holding true depth for those who choose to seek it.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/a66b00930c90e94aa1ac018ed49cd4253d7eed52.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Where Bonds and Paths Begin[/b][/h3][p]Upon reaching [b]Earlwood[/b], the village and its inhabitants lie open before you. What awaits is a cast of characters, each with their own story to tell. NPC relationships are a core part of our design—in [i]Dimraeth[/i], you will forge friendships and pursue romance with those you meet, each bond unfolding through unique questlines and personal moments. We know that character relationships and romance are a vital part of the RPG experience, and we aim to deliver.[/p][p][/p][p]Throughout the first act, you will return to Earlwood often. After forays into the wilds, you’ll come back to share discoveries with familiar faces, craft new tools, and prepare for the road ahead. In this way, the village becomes both a sanctuary and a living thread through your journey—a place where relationships deepen, and where each return carries new meaning.[/p][p][/p][p]Each return will also mark a pause between the dangers faced beyond the village. The world outside Earlwood is not a gentle one, and what you encounter there will shape both your path and those you come to know.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/06ccb9dd6606bb3e1a3fc7a12e2ef437f8159eeb.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Until Next Time…[/b][/h3][p]I’ll leave you with this: a simple dusk in Earlwood. Smoke curling from chimneys. A small circle of children and squirrels gathered near old [b]Befr[/b], begging for one more story before nightfall.[/p][p][/p][p]These are the moments worth protecting. The ones that remind us why we stand.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44028086/00b5a99630dfcb9c3813d407e7ca39705586d58a.png"][/img][/p][p]We’d be glad to share more of these glimpses behind the curtain, especially if you’re drawn to the deeper layers of the world — the craft of NPC design, the rationale behind the game loop, the shaping of biomes, the hidden threads of monster ecology, and more. If there are corners of [i]Dimraeth[/i] you’d like to hear more about, let us know.[/p][p][/p][p]For now, it’s back to the work of building. Thank you for reading. I look forward to the day we’ll meet in [b]Mirkea[/b].[/p][p]
[/p][p]Phillip
Game Director, [i]Dimraeth[/i][/p]
